* 1 cup of fresh blueberries
* 1 cup of fresh blackberries
* 1 cup of fresh honey
* 1 cup of fresh mint leaves

To cook these chocolate chip cookies, you will need to preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat. In a large mixing bowl, combine the butter, sugar, and brown sugar until creamy. Add in the eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition. In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined. Stir in the chocolate chips.

Using a cookie scoop or spoon, drop the dough by rounded tablespoons onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them about 2 inches apart. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden brown and the centers are set. Remove from the oven and let cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely. Enjoy your delicious chocolate chip cookies!

The disease depicted in the image is called "Gummosis" or "Bacterial Canker" and it affects the bark of trees, particularly fruit trees. It is caused by a bacterial infection, usually by the bacterium Pseudomonas syringae, which enters the tree through wounds or natural openings in the bark. The bacteria produce a toxin that causes the tree to produce excessive amounts of gum, which can be seen as a yellow, orange, or brown substance oozing from the tree.

Treatment for Gummosis involves preventing the spread of the disease and managing the symptoms. Pruning away infected branches and removing any dead or dying tissue can help prevent the spread of the disease. Additionally, applying a copper-based fungicide to the tree can help prevent the growth of the bacteria and reduce the amount of gum produced. It is important to note that Gummosis can weaken the tree and make it more susceptible to other diseases, so it is crucial to monitor the tree's health and take appropriate action if the disease recurs.
